accepted.s: Murshid Quli Khan is associated with which one of the following administrative changes in Bengal?
o: Shifting the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad
Shifting the capital from Murshidabad to Dacca
Shifting the capital from Calcutta to Dacca
Shifting the capital from Patna to Murshidabad
accepted.x: Murshid Quli Khan shifted the capital of Bengal from Dacca to Murshidabad.
accepted.tq: Test the location change directly by distinguishing the old capital from the new one.
accepted.sec: Murshid Quli Khan - capital shift, revenue reforms (mal jasmani, ijaradari)

accepted.s: The term ‘ijaradari’ in the revenue administration of Bengal refers to
o: Collection of land revenue through contractors
Collection of customs duties only from European companies
Direct collection of revenue by village headmen
Assignment of jagirs exclusively to Mughal princes
accepted.x: Under ijaradari, contractors called ij aradars collected land revenue. The system is also linked with the contract-based collection described as mal jasmani.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a revenue-collection method and unrelated forms of land assignment or customs collection.
accepted.sec: Murshid Quli Khan - capital shift, revenue reforms (mal jasmani, ijaradari)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the term ‘mal jasmani’ in the context of Bengal revenue administration?
o: A grant of tax-free land to religious institutions
A military tax imposed on European traders
A contract-based system of revenue collection
A system of cash payment to Mughal soldiers
accepted.x: The term mal jasmani is used for the contract-based revenue-collection arrangement associated with ijaradari.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a similar-sounding administrative term rather than its wider historical context.
accepted.sec: Murshid Quli Khan - capital shift, revenue reforms (mal jasmani, ijaradari)

accepted.s: What was the principal significance of converting jagir land into khalisa under Murshid Quli Khan?
o: It transferred the land permanently to the English Company
It converted the land into private property of the zamindars
It exempted the land from all forms of revenue
It placed the land under direct state revenue administration
accepted.x: Conversion of jagir land into khalisa brought the land under direct state control for revenue purposes.
accepted.tq: Apply the distinction between assigned jagir land and directly administered khalisa land.
accepted.sec: Murshid Quli Khan - capital shift, revenue reforms (mal jasmani, ijaradari)

accepted.s: Murshid Quli Khan’s demand from the English was related to
o: Withdrawal of all English troops from Bengal
Transfer of the English factory to Murshidabad
Payment of tribute to the French
accepted.x: Murshid Quli Khan wanted the English to pay customs duties, but the English increased their military establishment instead.
accepted.tq: Link the Nawab’s fiscal demand with the Company’s contrasting military response.
accepted.sec: Murshid Quli Khan - capital shift, revenue reforms (mal jasmani, ijaradari)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Siraj-ud-Daula — Last independent Nawab of Bengal
Robert Clive — Founder of the British Empire in India
Mir Jafar — Founder of the autonomous Bengal Nawabi
accepted.x: Mir Jafar was the puppet Nawab installed after Plassey. The autonomous Bengal Nawabi was founded by Murshid Quli Khan.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped title by matching each person with the precise designation associated with him.
accepted.sec: PERSON - called as / known as

accepted.s:
Arrange the Nawabs of Bengal in the correct chronological order of their rule:
A. Alivardi Khan
B. Shuja-ud-din
C. Siraj-ud-Daula
D. Sarfaraz Khan
accepted.x: The correct order is Shuja-ud-din, Sarfaraz Khan, Alivardi Khan and Siraj-ud-Daula.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence by using the regnal periods 1727–39, 1739–40, 1740–56 and 1756–57.
accepted.sec: Nawabs of Bengal in order → key act and Mughal status

accepted.s: Which Nawab of Bengal was the son-in-law of Murshid Quli Khan?
accepted.x: Shuja-ud-din was the son-in-law of Murshid Quli Khan. Sarfaraz Khan was Shuja-ud-din’s son and Murshid Quli Khan’s grandson.
accepted.tq: Use family relationships to distinguish the two successive Nawabs connected with Murshid Quli Khan.
accepted.sec: Nawabs of Bengal in order → key act and Mughal status

accepted.s: Sarfaraz Khan was defeated and killed by Alivardi Khan in the
accepted.x: Alivardi Khan seized the throne after killing Sarfaraz Khan in the Battle of Giria in 1740.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–battle association, a common trap in medieval and modern Indian history.
accepted.sec: Nawabs of Bengal in order → key act and Mughal status

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Alivardi Khan had served as Deputy Governor of Bihar.
2. Alivardi Khan banned English and French fortification of Calcutta and Chandernagore.
3. Siraj-ud-Daula was the grandson of Alivardi Khan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Alivardi Khan was Deputy Governor of Bihar, opposed the fortification of Calcutta and Chandernagore, and was succeeded by his grandson Siraj-ud-Daula.
accepted.tq: Check the office, policy and family relationship together before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Nawabs of Bengal in order → key act and Mughal status

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Siraj-ud-Daula is correct?
o: He installed Mir Jafar as Nawab after the Battle of Plassey.
He was the son of Shuja-ud-din and succeeded Alivardi Khan as his son.
He received an imperial farman as Subahdar of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
He was appointed as Governor of Bengal by the English Company.
accepted.x: Siraj-ud-Daula obtained an imperial farman as Subahdar of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. He was Alivardi Khan’s grandson, and Mir Jafar succeeded him after Plassey.
accepted.tq: Reject the family and succession reversals and identify the correct Mughal-status detail.
accepted.sec: Nawabs of Bengal in order → key act and Mughal status

accepted.s: The Battle of Plassey was fought between
accepted.x: Robert Clive led the English forces against Siraj-ud-Daula at Plassey.
accepted.tq: Identify the principal commanders without confusing the Nawab with his later successor or with the naval commander.
accepted.sec: Battle of Plassey - year, location, commanders, conspirators

accepted.s: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 on the bank of the
accepted.x: The battle was fought on 23 June 1757 at Plassey, also called Palashi, on the Bhagirathi River in present-day Nadia district of West Bengal.
accepted.tq: Combine the exact date with the river location to avoid confusing Plassey with other Bengal events.
accepted.sec: Battle of Plassey - year, location, commanders, conspirators

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a conspirator against Siraj-ud-Daula at Plassey?
accepted.x: Mir Madan was loyal to Siraj-ud-Daula and was not among the conspirators. Mir Jafar, Rai Durlabh and Jagat Seth were associated with the conspiracy.
accepted.tq: Find the loyal commander hidden among the names of the conspirators.
accepted.sec: Battle of Plassey - year, location, commanders, conspirators

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the forces at Plassey:
1. Robert Clive commanded approximately 3,000 men.
2. Siraj-ud-Daula’s force numbered approximately 50,000 men.
3. Siraj-ud-Daula’s forces received French support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Clive had about 3,000 men, while Siraj-ud-Daula had about 50,000 troops with French support.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical contrast and the allied-support detail to verify all three statements.
accepted.sec: Battle of Plassey - year, location, commanders, conspirators

accepted.s: Who among the following was loyal to Siraj-ud-Daula during the Battle of Plassey?
accepted.x: Mohan Lal, along with Mir Madan, remained loyal to Siraj-ud-Daula. Amir Chand, Manik Chand and Rai Durlabh were associated with the opposing conspiracy.
accepted.tq: Distinguish loyal commanders from the conspirators by testing one name from the opposing group.
accepted.sec: Battle of Plassey - year, location, commanders, conspirators

accepted.s: After the Battle of Plassey, which one of the following events took place?
o: Jagat Seth became the Subahdar of Bengal
Mir Jafar was made Nawab of Bengal
Siraj-ud-Daula became Nawab again with English support
Alivardi Khan was restored to the throne
accepted.x: Siraj-ud-Daula fled, was captured and executed, and Mir Jafar was installed as Nawab after Plassey.
accepted.tq: Test the immediate succession outcome rather than the military events preceding the battle.
accepted.sec: Battle of Plassey - year, location, commanders, conspirators

accepted.s:
Arrange the following battles in chronological order:
A. Plassey
B. Wandiwash
C. Ambur
D. Buxar
accepted.x: Ambur was fought in 1749, Plassey in 1757, Wandiwash in 1760 and Buxar in 1764.
accepted.tq: Place the battles by their years and then eliminate sequences with an incorrect first or middle event.
accepted.sec: Significance of Plassey - battle chronology, "first decisive" debate

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: St. Thome/Adyar was fought in 1746. Condore/Chandurti was fought in 1758, Chinsura/Bidara in 1759, and Buxar in 1764.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year–battle pair and reject the shifted dates in the remaining options.
accepted.sec: Significance of Plassey - battle chronology, "first decisive" debate

accepted.s:
With reference to the significance of Plassey, consider the following statements:
1. The battle transformed the English East India Company from a trading body into a political power.
2. Bengal’s wealth helped finance the defeat of the French.
3. Plassey was primarily a prolonged military contest in which the English defeated an equally matched army.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Plassey is generally viewed as a victory of treachery and a political-financial arrangement rather than a prolonged contest between equally matched armies.
accepted.tq: Identify the overstatement in the description of Plassey as an equally matched military contest.
accepted.sec: Significance of Plassey - battle chronology, "first decisive" debate

accepted.s: Which battle is treated as the real military test that confirmed the result of Plassey?
accepted.x: Buxar, fought in 1764, is regarded as the real military test and confirmed the political result achieved at Plassey.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the politically decisive Plassey from the later battle regarded as the decisive military test.
accepted.sec: Significance of Plassey - battle chronology, "first decisive" debate

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the debate regarding the ‘first decisive’ battle in the establishment of British power?
o: Plassey is usually called the foundation of British rule, while Buxar is treated as the most significant or decisive battle in some assessments.
Plassey is never considered important in the establishment of British rule.
Buxar occurred before Plassey and caused the installation of Mir Jafar.
Wandiwash alone established British political authority over Bengal.
accepted.x: Plassey is commonly called the foundation of British rule, but Buxar is treated in some examination assessments as the most significant or decisive battle.
accepted.tq: Separate the conventional description of Plassey from the alternative assessment of Buxar’s military significance.
accepted.sec: Significance of Plassey - battle chronology, "first decisive" debate

accepted.s: The English misuse of dastaks primarily resulted in
o: Transfer of Calcutta to the French
Recognition of Mir Jafar as Subahdar
Loss of revenue to the Nawab
accepted.x: The 1717 farman allowed duty-free Company trade, but Company servants misused dastaks for private trade, causing the Nawab to lose revenue.
accepted.tq: Connect the misuse of a fiscal privilege with its direct administrative consequence.
accepted.sec: Causes of conflict - dastak misuse, fortification of Calcutta, fugitives

accepted.s: The farman of 1717 was issued during the reign of
accepted.x: The 1717 farman associated with duty-free trade for the Company was issued by Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–farman association and avoid substituting another Mughal emperor.
accepted.sec: Causes of conflict - dastak misuse, fortification of Calcutta, fugitives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of conflict between Siraj-ud-Daula and the English:
1. The English fortified Fort William without the Nawab’s permission.
2. The French obeyed Siraj’s order to stop fortification, whereas the English did not.
3. The English provided asylum to Krishna Das, a fugitive from the Nawab.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three developments intensified the conflict: unauthorised fortification, English refusal to stop it, and asylum to Krishna Das.
accepted.tq: Group the fiscal, military and asylum-related causes and check each against the Nawab’s objections.
accepted.sec: Causes of conflict - dastak misuse, fortification of Calcutta, fugitives

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of court factions was associated with English support during the conflict with Siraj-ud-Daula?
o: Ghaseti Begum and Shaukat Jang of Purnea
accepted.x: Ghaseti Begum and Shaukat Jang of Purnea were court factions whom the English were perceived to support against Siraj-ud-Daula.
accepted.tq: Match the political factions with the correct side instead of confusing them with military officers or English officials.
accepted.sec: Causes of conflict - dastak misuse, fortification of Calcutta, fugitives

accepted.s: The Black Hole episode is said to have occurred on
accepted.x: The episode is traditionally said to have occurred on 20 June 1756 after Siraj-ud-Daula captured Fort William.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of the Black Hole episode from the date of the Battle of Plassey.
accepted.sec: Black Hole episode - narrator, historiographical debate

accepted.s: Who narrated the Black Hole episode and was himself regarded as one of the survivors?
accepted.x: J.Z. Holwell, one of the survivors, gave the principal account on which the story of the Black Hole largely rests.
accepted.tq: Identify the narrator by separating the eyewitness account from the military and administrative figures involved.
accepted.sec: Black Hole episode - narrator, historiographical debate

accepted.s: According to the traditional account of the Black Hole episode, which one of the following combinations is correct?
accepted.x: The traditional account states that 146 English prisoners were confined in a small cell and about 120 died. Holwell’s own figure for the deaths was 123.
accepted.tq: Keep the traditional figures separate from Holwell’s distinct figure for the deaths.
accepted.sec: Black Hole episode - narrator, historiographical debate

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Black Hole episode is correct?
o: Historians have doubted the reported numbers, and the British used the story to justify war.
The episode occurred after Clive recaptured Calcutta in 1757.
The reported numbers have been accepted without historical question.
The episode was narrated by Siraj-ud-Daula after the Battle of Plassey.
accepted.x: Historians have questioned the reported numbers, while the British used the episode as a justification for war against Bengal.
accepted.tq: Test the historiographical qualification rather than accepting the traditional narrative uncritically.
accepted.sec: Black Hole episode - narrator, historiographical debate

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Calcutta was recaptured by Clive and Watson
B. Kasimbazar factory was seized
C. Calcutta fell to Siraj-ud-Daula
D. Treaty of Alinagar was concluded
accepted.x: Kasimbazar was seized in May 1756, Calcutta fell in June 1756, Clive and Watson recaptured it in January 1757, and the Treaty of Alinagar followed in February 1757.
accepted.tq: Use the month sequence from May 1756 through February 1757 to arrange the events.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey

accepted.s: During the fall of Calcutta in 1756, which one of the following correctly describes the actions of the English officials?
o: Drake and Holwell defended Chandernagore against Siraj.
Governor Drake surrendered and Holwell fled to Fulta.
Governor Drake fled to Fulta and Holwell surrendered.
Both Drake and Holwell escaped to Madras before the attack.
accepted.x: Governor Drake fled to Fulta, while Holwell surrendered when Calcutta fell to Siraj-ud-Daula.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the actions of two officials involved in the fall of Calcutta.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey

accepted.s: Clive and Admiral Watson recaptured Calcutta in January 1757 after coming from
accepted.x: Clive and Admiral Watson came from Madras and recaptured Calcutta in January 1757.
accepted.tq: Test the origin of the recapturing force while avoiding confusion with the French settlement of Chandernagore.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey

accepted.s: The Treaty of Alinagar, concluded in February 1757, restored the Company’s
o: French trading rights and prohibited English fortification
1717 privileges and permitted the fortification of Calcutta
1740 privileges and transferred Murshidabad to the Company
1764 privileges and granted the Diwani of Bengal
accepted.x: The Treaty of Alinagar restored the Company’s privileges under the 1717 arrangement and allowed it to fortify Calcutta.
accepted.tq: Match the treaty with its specific privileges and avoid attributing the later Diwani settlement to it.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey

accepted.s: After the Treaty of Alinagar, Robert Clive captured
accepted.x: After the Treaty of Alinagar, Clive captured the French settlement of Chandernagore.
accepted.tq: Track the immediate post-treaty action and distinguish the French settlement from English and Nawabi centres.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey

accepted.s: Which one of the following was included among the rewards received by the English Company after Plassey?
o: The whole of the Carnatic as a jagir
The fort of Chandernagore from Mir Jafar
accepted.x: The Company received the Zamindari of the 24 Parganas, along with duty-free trade privileges and monetary payments.
accepted.tq: Identify the territorial reward directly associated with Plassey and reject unrelated regional concessions.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey

accepted.s: Mir Jafar paid the English Company approximately
accepted.x: Mir Jafar paid the Company Rs 1,77,00,000 after Plassey.
accepted.tq: Read the Indian-numbering figure carefully and distinguish one crore seventy-seven lakh from smaller amounts.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey

accepted.s: The duty-free trade privileges obtained by the Company after Plassey covered
accepted.x: The Company obtained duty-free trade in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa as part of the rewards following Plassey.
accepted.tq: Compare the geographical extent of the trading privilege with neighbouring regions not included in it.
accepted.sec: Siraj's capture of Calcutta, Clive-Watson recapture, rewards of Plassey
